Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1141 Of 2025
 Vinod G. Dcosta ...Applicant
 V/s.
 The State of Maharashtra ...Respondent.

With
 Interim Application No. 3623 Of 2025
 ..............
 Mr. Arvind Tiwari for the Applicant.
Mr. B.V. Holambe Patil, App for the Respondent/State.

Mr. Shekhar Jagtap i/b Mr. Tanmay Tendulkar for the
 Intervener in Ia.
 Api Santosh Munde, Byculla Police Station is present.
This is an application for anticipatory bail.

2.  The applicant is apprehending his arrest in Crime No. 499 of 2024 registered at Byculla Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
3.

According to the prosecution, the applicant and other co- accused induced the first informant, his relatives and other investors to invest money in stock market and forex trading by assuring them of profitable returns on their investment.
It is alleged that the first informant and other investors transferred amount of Rs.1,74,80,000/- to the applicant's bank account.
It is further alleged that the applicant neither returned the invested amounts nor provided the assured benefits to the first informant 4-aba-1141-25@ia.doc and the other investors.

The allegations against the applicant and other co-accused are thus of defrauding the first informant and other investors to the tune of Anthony Francis Dais vs State Of Maharashtra on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82299192/
1 Rs.1,74,80,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the applicant, the learned APP for the respondent / State and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2/intervenor.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that certain amount was repaid to the investors and thus it cannot be said that since inception the intention of the applicant was to cheat the first informant and other investors.
It is submitted that there is no need of custodial interrogation and the applicant is ready and willing to cooperate in the investigation.
6. On the other hand, learned APP for the respondent/State and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submit that there are in all 23 investors and that no amount has been repaid to them.
It is submitted that considering the nature of crime, the applicant may not be released on anticipatory bail.
7. The applicant has not placed on record a single document to show that he invested the amount of investors in stock market and forex trading.
In that view of the matter, I am not inclined to release the applicant on anticipatory bail.

The Application is therefore, rejected.
8.
The Interim Application stands disposed of.

[N.R.BORKAR, J.]
